newsitem.title: UK: T-bonds rise slightly in London ahead of holiday.
newsitem.headline: T-bonds rise slightly in London ahead of holiday.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries were slightly higher in London on Friday ahead of Monday's holiday in the U.S. as the market took a calmer view of a Fed official's comments on inflation.
By 1145 GMT, the 30-year long bond was at 95-26, up from 95-23 in Tokyo and 95-25 in New York.
A trader at a U.S. bank said the market was quiet ahead of Martin Luther King Day on Monday.
"There has been some selling off in what I think are wrong expectations of some liquidation of long positions," the trader said.
An economist at another U.S. bank said the market had regained its composure after Fed Governor Laurence Meyer made a series of remarks seen at first as hawkish on inflation.
The economist said Meyer's comments, voicing some concern about the risk of inflation, had put the market on the alert to the possibility of rate rises.
But the negative follow-through reaction had been relatively muted as traders took a second reading of Meyer's speech, he said.
He said the market would scrutinise trade data for November at 1330 GMT for any light it could shed on the 1996 fourth quarter GDP number which is due later this month.
The trade data was expected to show a deficit of $9.8 billion against an $8.0 billion shortfall in October.
"If the trade deficit is small, that will encourage the perception that growth in the U.S. is going to be strong and may put some further upward pressure on yields," the economist said.
"If we get a narrow trade deficit and a strong capacity utilisation figure, that may put some further pressure on the bond market."
December industrial production data, due at 1415 GMT, is forecast to show a 0.6 percent rise after a 0.9 percent increase in November.
Capacity utilisation for the same month, also at 1415 GMT, is forecast at 83.5 percent, up from 83.3 percent previously.
The economist said a narrow trade deficit and a strong capacity utilisation figure might together put further pressure on the bond market.
However, the trader said the only data that mattered on Fridays was non-farm payroll figures.
The trader expected little excitement for the rest of the day and that March T-bonds would "wash around 110-16, probably closing around 110-28,30."
